title: Ouverture
subtitle: The overture to Die Zauberflöte, in Gustav F. Kogel's piano reduction

licences.source: W. A. Mozart, Die Zauberflöte, K. 620 (1791), Ouverture (overture), before Act 1 No. 1
licences.author: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756–1791)

licences.source: Edition Peters vocal score, piano reduction by Gustav F. Kogel (Leipzig, plate 7794; IMSLP #225460), pages 3–9 (226 bars)
licences.author: Gustav F. Kogel, piano reduction as printed
licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages: each half (pages 3–6 and 7–9) read by two independent readers, with a judge settling every difference and a sweep for the marks, then stitched and checked bar by bar by three fresh proofreaders, and checked against the print again; every bar adds up. Adagio in C (4/4), E-flat major, bars 1–15; Allegro, bars 16–96; Adagio, bars 97–102: the threefold chord, three wind chords each followed by a fermata on the rest; Allegro, bars 103–226. Instrument cues (G.Orch., Fl., Ob., Clar., Fag., Harm., Streich. …) and fingerings are left out; single-chord tremolo strokes are written as held chords; a few ties and slurs that pass from one voice to another in the print may not show; dynamics printed between the staves are given to both hands. Playback tempo: Allegro ♩ = 180 (half note = 90), Adagio ♩ = 60 (a third of the Allegro's beat, so the introduction takes about a minute), fermatas held; about 6 minutes in all, the median (6:00) of five complete recordings (Norrington 5:51, Christie 1995 5:57, Jacobs 2010 6:00, Klemperer 1964 7:17, Haitink 1981 7:33). Mozart gives the words only.
